manifests.rationale: Round 15: source-to-target permutation control for the conditional layer-10 MLP fit.

Round 10: opposite-sign control for the fixed layer-10 sparse norm-gain fit; absolute W0-relative replacement.

Round 27: predeclared fourfold dose of the fixed sparse block-33 MLP output-gain correction.
Round 19: preselected, norm-matched layer-7 head-4 attenuation control.
Round 11: test specificity of the fitted coordinate-to-offset assignment by a fixed seeded permutation, reconstructed from W0.
Round 13: fourfold-strength test of the fixed context-dependent layer-10 MLP correction, reconstructed from W0.

Round 3: preplanned weak-dose test. Absolute replacement of the same tensor reconstructed from W0, not cumulative editing.

Round 25: preselected disjoint matched-column control for the conditional layer-33 MLP correction.
Round 4: opposite-sign causal control; same layer, channels and direction, W0-relative rather than compounded.
Round 28: predeclared opposite-sign control for the sparse final-block gain correction.

Round 1: test whether suppressing opposing MLP writes at the strongest cross-source residual-localization site reduces instruction-sensitive spatial overcounting. No claim of a universal spatial or zero-count mechanism.
Round 14: equal-strength opposite-sign control for the context-dependent layer-10 MLP patch.
Round 8: revised answer-balanced hypothesis. Test sparse nonuniform layer-10 post-MLP norm gains after normalized branch captures showed more consistency than raw writes.
Round 12: bounded context-dependent layer-10 MLP write correction using only reproduced failure/success contrasts.
Round 24: source-to-target permutation control for the gain-aware conditional layer-33 MLP fit.
Round 21: bounded, gain-aware conditional correction of the final decoder MLP write, reconstructed from W0.
Round 30: predeclared disjoint matched-coordinate control for the sparse final-block gain correction.
Round 23: predeclared equal-strength opposite-sign control for the conditional layer-33 MLP correction.
Dose test of the modestly beneficial attention intervention, seeking reduced control damage rather than assuming its score gain validates the initial failure mechanism.
Sign-specific control for the layer-10 attention intervention; rebuild the sole edited tensor from W0.
Round 18: opposite-direction control for layer-15 MLP projection removal, rebuilt from W0 rather than accumulated.
Substantial dose stress test of the weakened layer-26 directional-write hypothesis, with all other weights exactly W0.
Round 19: fixed-seed random-output-direction control for the layer-15 MLP intervention, reconstructed from W0.
Round 21: preregistered matched-channel ablation control for round 20, independently reconstructed from W0.
Complete half/removal/reflection dose comparison for the observed layer-10 attention effect; the half-dose safety prediction failed.
Matched random-channel control holding output direction and edit coefficient magnitudes/signs fixed.
Test earlier attention-output involvement after late-MLP direction attenuation and its sign control were behaviorally null.
Matched random-output-direction control, holding selected attention channels and input coefficients fixed.
Round 17: independently test the controlled layer-15 MLP contrast after the attention-component decomposition failed to retain focal visual repairs.

Round 10: second fixed-seed, norm-matched random-output-direction control. The sole edited tensor is rebuilt from W0, not accumulated from the parent. Preserve the unresolved discrepancies between cached evaluation and fresh diagnostic responses.
Round 16: evaluate the exact complement of the head-7 component. Rebuild from W0 so the head-7 edit is absent rather than retained cumulatively.

Round 22: separate the broader selected-channel ablation from removal of the nominated output direction by retaining the parallel component and removing its orthogonal complement, independently reconstructed from W0.

Round 11: second fixed-seed matched-channel control, rebuilt from W0. Test whether the originally selected channels outperform comparable alternatives rather than interpreting isolated anchor repairs as specific evidence.
Round 20: full-column ablation of the 64 selected layer-15 MLP channels to test their broader contribution after directional interventions failed the focal prediction.
Round 15: isolate the exact head-7 portion of round 4's edit, without rescaling. This is a structural decomposition, not a claim that head 7 encodes object size.
Opposite-sign control for rounds 1 and 2. The sole edited tensor is rebuilt from W0, so this is not a cumulative dose.
Round 14: ablate the previously fixed matched alternative-channel set to test whether round 13's benefits require the originally selected channel identities. Reconstruct the tensor from W0.

Test whether selectively attenuating late MLP writes opposing a controlled success/failure direction improves order-sensitive counterfactual visual answers. This is an unvalidated mechanistic hypothesis, not a finding.

Round 13: complete ablation of the 64 originally selected layer-10 attention-output columns. Test their broader causal contribution after small directional and orthogonal interventions yielded limited, nonspecific changes.
Round 12: matched-norm orthogonal-component control on the original 64 attention-output columns, reconstructed from W0. Test direction specificity beyond random-sign controls.
